smell_validity.evidence: A complete predecessor output pipeline - layout module, interface renderers, row builder, text helpers, printer emitter - is retained with no supported configuration reaching it, while live modules still import parts, so removal is a reachability decision, not a listing. Its live namesake renderers differ only by dispatch, making the retained-obsolete-implementation fault unmistakable and consequential.

maintenance_impact.evidence: The retired pipeline claims the same vocabulary as the live overlays, so any output-format change forces a which-pipeline decision; a hand-synced duplicate field list and import edges that execute dead module code at startup deepen the trap. Deleting restores one owner per row format. Gains are strong but confined to one output subsystem, not architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Vocabulary, filters, output idioms and helper reuse grow naturally from the live renderers, and import-only wiring convincingly models an unfinished migration. But the additions uniformly self-annotate their retirement in docstrings, and the pipeline's own TSV rows contradict its stated fixed-width purpose - tells that ordinary repository evolution would rarely show.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names the predecessor design, all five remnant clusters, the sweep of orphaned imports, an exact preservation boundary, and the decisive reachability question. It directly forecloses the costliest misrepair - deleting the live lookalike overlays, which no test observes - and warns against registry and attribute-dispatch shortcuts. Residual edge: unrelated pre-existing dead helpers only implicitly excluded.

semantic_diversity.evidence: At least three purposes require different decisions: deleting orphaned entry points, removing transitively-referenced helpers, surgically pruning shared import lines while preserving live co-imports, and sparing helpers dead code shares with live renderers. One reachability criterion governs the deletions though, so purposes need varied evidence rather than a genuinely different repair each.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names clusters, not symbols; one domain-word search plus a call-chain walk reaches every remnant. Classification is the real burden: the dead builder looks exactly like registry-driven live handler classes, dead entry points sit beside live lookalikes, and live-module import edges mask deadness. Resolving these combines multiple components' behavior, though not two chained indirect mechanisms.

repair_coordination.evidence: A shared rule binds every location: a removed definition's remaining import or cross-module reference must vanish in the same change. Deleting the layout module or builder without pruning the live import lines breaks package import on every run. Many sites are otherwise independent; no interlocking rule pair or ordering constraint beyond reference consistency exists.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Only the two orphan entry points - under 20% of sites - fall to single-pass unreferenced-definition deletion; import edges and intra-pipeline references mask everything else, and unused-import detection finds nothing while intact. Token-keyed deletion misses most clusters and strands imports that break startup; iterative extension misclassifies live attribute-dispatched code and still cannot delete the module file.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Two hidden failure paths: deleting the live lookalike overlays, or over-pruning the shared import lines beside live names - the suite exercises no machine-readable overlay, so both stay green while ordinary flagged CLI calls crash afterward. No interacting-stage or state-dependent failure is established, and some other wrong edits fail loudly at import time.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
